subject: Production: Hemisphere Health - US-WEST2 500s & latency — failover coordination
messages:
From: Jim Pattinson <jim.p@hemispherehealth.com>
To: support@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Kira O'Neill <kira.oneill@hemispherehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: sustained 500s + latency spike - US-WEST2

Hi Redwood team,

We started seeing a sustained stream of 500 responses and high tail latency from the Redwood endpoint servicing our UH-telemetry pipeline in US-WEST2 at ~09:05 PDT. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~9% and p99 latency climbed from 450ms to >6s. This is impacting ingestion and downstream analytics.

Can you confirm if there was any known maintenance/region issue or a routing change on your side? Attached is a short snapshot of our request traces and a representative curl to your API showing repeated 500s.

Attachments: sample-trace-09-05.json (json), hh-request-sample.txt (txt)

We need an ETA for mitigation and whether you plan to route traffic off US-WEST2 — our SLAs require prompt notification.

Thanks,
Jim Pattinson
VP Engineering, Hemisphere Health
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Jim Pattinson <jim.p@hemispherehealth.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 07 Jun 2028 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: sustained 500s + latency spike - US-WEST2

Hi Jim — thanks for the signal and the traces. We're on it.

Quick status:
- Triage started (SRE paged) — initial suspects are a hot partition in the US-WEST2 KV cache and a recent autoscaler adjustment.
- We're collecting heap and request-level diagnostics now.

Immediate next steps:
1) Rishi's team will validate whether a regional eviction/redispatch is required.
2) If we can't stabilize within 20 minutes, we'll initiate cross-region steering to US-EAST-1 and US-WEST-1 for read traffic and hold write paths behind a circuit breaker.

I'll keep you updated every 15 minutes.

—Laura
Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: triage-loghead-09-20.txt (txt)
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 07 Jun 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Production: sustained 500s + latency spike - US-WEST2

Confirming findings from the diagnostics run:
- Observed KV cache eviction thrash on a subset of hosts (node-set usw2-gpu-pool-3). Memory pressure + a buggy kernel path in the quantized runtime resulted in increased tail latency and 500s when cache misses spiked.
- Autoscaler bumped capacity repeatedly which amplified cold-start pressure and KV churn.

Mitigation performed at 09:40 PDT:
- Isolated the faulty host group and removed from routing (soft drain).
- Applied a temporary hot-key throttling rule for the HH workload prefix.
- Rolling restart of 6 affected serving pods.

Recommended next action (if p99 > 1.5s after 10m): initiate controlled geo-evacuation (traffic-steer) to US-EAST-1 with sticky session pinning for current connections. This reduces tail risk while preserving throughput.

Diagnostics bundle uploaded: redwood_diagnostics_20280607.tar.gz
Runbook reference: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/geo-evac-guide (see section 4.2 emergency steering)

I'll start a failover plan if we don't see stabilization by 09:55.
—Rishi
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Jonas / Marissa — forwarding the thread for exec visibility. TL;DR: Hemisphere Health is experiencing elevated 500s & p99 latency from US-WEST2 due to a KV cache eviction bug + autoscaler interactions. SRE has isolated hosts and started rolling restarts; might need geo-steer to US-EAST-1 if tail latency doesn't recover in the next 20 minutes.

Key asks:
- Approval to execute a controlled geo-evacuation (traffic-steer) to US-EAST-1 including temporary write hold behind a circuit breaker — this will introduce a brief destabilization window but reduces ongoing error-rate risk.
- Authorization for a 24-hour service credit if Hemisphere requests it (they're enterprise, sensitive to QTD analytics jobs).

If you prefer, I can join a 10:05 bridge with HH; otherwise proceed with SRE recommendation at 10:00.

—Vivek
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Cc: Kira O'Neill <kira.oneill@hemispherehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Production: sustained 500s + latency spike - US-WEST2

Thanks — we see errors dropping after your changes at ~09:50 and p99 is back under 800ms for most endpoints. Appreciate the quick triage.

Two asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm whether you plan to do a full cross-region drain to US-EAST-1 or hold the soft-drain as a contingency? We need to know before running QTD batch jobs at 11:00.
2) We would like a short RCA and a timeline for the permanent fix; also please advise on compensation/credits for the window where retries spiked.

Kira is available for a 10:45 bridge if needed.

—Jim
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Production: sustained 500s + latency spike - US-WEST2 — next steps

Thanks Jim — good to hear the immediate metrics rebounded. Finalizing plan and commitments below:

Short-term (next 24h):
- Keep the affected host group soft-drained and maintain hot-key throttling rule.
- No full cross-region drain for now; we'll keep geo-steer as a hot action if p99 rises above 1.5s.
- SRE to share mitigations and the diagnostics bundle (done).
- Customer is eligible for goodwill credit: approved 24 hours pro-rated service credit contingent on formal RCA (approved by Vivek).

Mid-term (1–2 weeks):
- Engineering will patch the kernel path causing KV churn and validate in a canary pool.
- We'll provide you a written RCA and timeline for the fix by EOD Friday.

Actions:
- Rishi: produce concise RCA draft and remediation ETA (owner) — due: 2028-06-09 EOD.
- Laura: schedule a 30-minute bridge for 10:45 if HH wants to join; otherwise send summary email.
- Aditya/Vivek: handle commercial note and coordinate credit issuance.

Attachments: runbook-eu-failover-v2.pdf (pdf), incident-graphs-09-05.png (png)

—Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
